text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-Oslo's police force has been forced to make dramatic cost cuts. The consequences are particularly serious in the narcotics unit, which must reduce spending by 60 percent compared with 1996.
-Top Norwegian skier Kjetil-Andre Aamodt collected the fourth gold medal of his career on Thursday when he won the men's combined at the Alpine skiing world championships in Sestriere, Italy.

-Central Bank Governor Kjell Storvik said in his annual sppech on Thursday that it is still his goal to maintain a stable exchange rate for the runway crown. However, he conceded, it is difficult to fight the market.
-The government Statistics Bureau sees high economic growth over the next two years and inflation below two percent.
-Order reserves at engineering and construction group Kvaerner have increased sharply. During the last four months Kvaerner has signed contracts worth 24 billion crowns.
